messages:
Nadia Chen: Quick announce: CI/Auth migration kickoff tomorrow. This thread is for rollout notes, small-team blockers, and emergency contacts.
Rafael Ortiz: Scope recap? Which systems exactly are moving?
Nadia Chen: Jenkins -> GitHub Actions (org-level workflows, runner orchestration). Auth: LDAP/legacy SSO -> Okta SCIM + org-enforced SSO. Artifact access via CI service accounts will switch to short-lived tokens.
Maya Gupta: Timeline? Any blackout?
Nadia Chen: Rollout phases: phase1 (dry-run) Apr 30 18:00-20:00 UTC for non-prod repos; phase2 (prod opt-in) May 3 00:00-06:00 UTC; phase3 (enforce SSO + retire old tokens) May 10 22:00-02:00 UTC. Expect degraded CI during windows, not full outage.
engops-bot: Reminder: please file migration tickets by Apr 28 if you require manual porting. See https://go.redwood.internal/ci-migration-guide
Rafael Ortiz: Any automation for translating Jenkinsfile to Actions?
Nadia Chen: We have a translator tool for simple declarative pipelines (build/test/publish). Complex Groovy logic needs manual rework. Tool lives in infra-tools; run `bin/jenkins2actions --repo <org/repo>` and inspect output.
Maya Gupta: Service accounts: we use a few long-lived machine accounts for publishing images. How will that change?
Nadia Chen: Good catch. We're introducing ephemeral service tokens for runners. Process: create a short-lived OIDC token attached to the runner, exchange for registry creds. Long-lived machine accounts will be disabled after May 10. Security Bot: All teams must migrate to OIDC or org secrets by May 7 or CI publish steps will fail.
Rafael Ortiz: Will self-hosted runners still be supported? We have GPU jobs that need them.
Nadia Chen: Yes. Self-hosted runners supported but must run the new runner agent and use ephemeral credentials. We will publish a hardened runner image and a helm chart for k8s-runner fleets.
Maya Gupta: Any change to permissions model? I rely on repo-level PATs in scripts.
Nadia Chen: Move away from personal PATs. Use `GITHUB_TOKEN`, org-level secrets, or scheduled service tokens. We'll run a scan for hard-coded PATs and contact repo owners. Expected false-positive list will be posted.
Rafael Ortiz: Rollback plan if something breaks during phase2?
Nadia Chen: Rollback options: 1) Re-enable Jenkins workers for specific repos via infra toggle. 2) Revert org workflow templates we push. We will keep a snapshot of Jenkins state for 72h after each phase. Contact SRE runbook on-call if urgent.
engops-bot: Maintenance scheduled by Nadia Chen: CI/Auth consolidation. Phase1: 2024-04-30 18:00 UTC.
Maya Gupta: Training/Docs? I have interns who need a quick primer.
Nadia Chen: We'll host two 45-minute sessions Apr 29 (EMEA-friendly) and Apr 30 (PT friendly). Slides + example repos will be uploaded. Also a migration checklist: 1) remove PATs 2) add CODEOWNERS 3) validate actions in staging org 4) switch publish steps to `docker/login-action` + OIDC.
Security Bot: Policy update: after May 10, non-SSO GitHub access attempts will be blocked by org policy. Ensure Okta group mapping for contractors.
Rafael Ortiz: Who to ping for last-minute exemptions?
Nadia Chen: Ping #eng-infra and tag @Nadia. For infra-level exceptions (e.g., legacy prod integrations) open an SRE request with justification.
Maya Gupta: Noted. I'll queue our migration ticket and join the May 3 window.
Nadia Chen: Thanks all. Diffs and scripts will be pushed to infra-tools this evening. I'll pin a short checklist in #eng-infra.
